elements.quote: Although the issue of growing prevalence of obesity among women of reproductive age has been previously addressed in many LMICs, such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and India, the problem has been underestimated in Pakistan because of scarcity of relevant data and lack of focussed policy in place.
elements.reason: The introduction describes a gap/uncertainty (scarcity of relevant data and lack of focused policy in Pakistan), but it does not clearly describe the overall current state of knowledge and important uncertainties in a comprehensive way.

elements.quote: This review article was planned to highlight the nutrition transition in Pakistan by exploring the factors contributing to rise in overweight and obesity among women of reproductive age (15-49 years), and possible policy recommendation for policy-makers to deal with this challenge.
elements.reason: The introduction explains the need/importance for conducting the review by stating its purpose to investigate determinants and support policy recommendations.
No evidence was provided that cites or discusses similar systematic reviews and explains why a new/current review is needed as an update/replication.
The provided evidence does not indicate this is a review of intervention effects; it is about socio-economic, environmental and demographic determinants.
The provided evidence does not describe a complex intervention or delivery context requiring a logic model; it focuses on determinants and prevalence/risk factors.

elements.quote: The current study attempted to investigate the socio-economic, environmental and demographic determinants of rise in obesity among women of reproductive years (15-49 years) in Pakistan.
